current.text: OKC traded away Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins, mostly for financial reasons, and took back no salary.
The trades cut a projected 240 million USD luxury tax bill to 20 million USD and brought in seven second-round picks.
No veteran was added to replace them. Their minutes go to rookies and unproven young players.
The rotation stays deep even after these losses.
The departures open up usage for the players who remain.
The Thunder will have to give more minutes to Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain.
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is doing more off-ball work. The expert thinks this may be because Mitchell and McCain need more minutes.
Cason Wallace is almost certainly going to start. The depth chart lists him as the starting SG.
Cason Wallace and Ajay Mitchell play a lot of minutes.
Guard minutes go to Gilgeous-Alexander, Mitchell, Wallace and Topic.
The center rotation is Isaiah Hartenstein, Chet Holmgren and Jaylin Williams.
Jaylin Williams barely played unless the centers were out.
Hartenstein's starting role looks secure.
The frontcourt is crowded with Holmgren, Al Horford (re-signed), Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams and Thomas Sorber. This limits minutes for rookie big men right away.
The Thunder are unsure about Hartenstein's future and about how Sarr will develop.
Apart from Jalen Williams and Alex Caruso, the team has no true wings who can guard bigger forwards.
The team may become less elite on defense and more focused on offense, with Gilgeous-Alexander, Mitchell and Jalen Williams playing together.
Without Joe, Dort and Wiggins, OKC will not repeat its share of roughly 37% of shots from three.
OKC is projected for about 62 wins (range 57 to 62). It has the best win total in the league, and OKC and San Antonio should be the top two seeds in the West.
OKC has the fewest back-to-backs in the league, so rest risk for its stars is lower.
The fantasy playoff schedule is strong: 11 games (rank 4 of 30) with only two back-to-back pairs, and none in week 19.

note: OKC is the best team in the league on paper. It has the fewest back-to-backs and a strong playoff schedule, so Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Holmgren carry little rest risk. The players who gain from the loss of Dort, Joe and Wiggins are Cason Wallace (likely starter), Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain, while Hartenstein's center role looks secure and the crowded frontcourt caps rookie bigs like Aday Mara. Early on, watch how much off-ball work Gilgeous-Alexander does and how the guard minutes split between Mitchell, McCain and Topic.
